transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-10-12 15:00 PT — Duration: 42 mins
Attendees: Alex Reed (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Tom Hartwell (CTO, Hartwell Pharma), Maya Chen (Head of Security), Leo Park (Infra Lead)

Auto-generated summary: initial security discovery; topics SOC2/ISO, SSO, RBAC, audit logs, KMS, data retention.

00:00 Alex Reed: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick round — Alex from Redwood, Priya is our solutions engineer. you good to go, Tom?
00:10 Tom Hartwell: Yeah hi, thanks. we are evaluating options — specifically security posture for hosted vs dedicated vs private. want to understand controls and where we land for compliance.
00:25 Maya Chen: hi all, maya here. main things for us: SOC 2, ISO 27001 evidence, SSO with SAML, RBAC, audit trails, encryption keys (we use a KMS), and data retention/purge rules.
00:40 Priya Nair: great, that's exactly what we typically cover. quick high level — Redwood offers hosted API, dedicated reserved capacity, and private (VPC/on-prem). each has different controls around networking and customer-managed keys.
00:56 Alex Reed: and i'll add we have SOC 2 Type II report and an ISO attestation summary we can share, and our hosted offering has encryption at rest with provider-managed keys by default.
01:10 Maya Chen: curious about KMS — do you support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key)? especially for private deployments?
01:20 Priya Nair: yes, for private we generally support customer-managed KMS integration; for dedicated we can do KMS integration options depending on contract; hosted default is provider-managed but we have enterprise tiers that allow BYOK.
01:36 Leo Park: network wise, if we go private we need a VPC peering or private link. what's the pattern — direct connect, vpn?
01:45 Priya Nair: typical patterns: VPC peering or PrivateLink for cloud, and for on-prem we offer a package that can be air-gapped. we'll share our network diagram.
01:56 Tom Hartwell: retention — we need logs retained for seven years for pharm regs, and also we need fine-grained audit logs of model inputs/outputs and who accessed them. is that supported?
02:10 Priya Nair: audit logs are available across all modes; retention policies can be configured, longer-term retention is an add-on in hosted, dedicated/private you can push to your S3 or SIEM. note: logging of PII and output — there are redaction controls and you can opt-out of persistence on hosted at rest but it's limited depending on plan.
02:35 Maya Chen: and RBAC — we have strict least-privilege access. does Redwood integrate with our SSO — we use Okta with SAML and SCIM for user provisioning.
02:48 Alex Reed: yes, we support SSO via SAML and OIDC and provisioning via SCIM. we'd like to see your IdP flows but it's supported.
03:02 Priya Nair: on roles we expose per-route and per-model roles; you can restrict who can call production models vs dev, and there's token-level controls.
03:15 Leo Park: want to dig into encryption in transit — TLS versions, cipher suites, mutual TLS?
03:23 Priya Nair: TLS 1.2+ supported; mutual TLS is available for private endpoints. we'll send the crypto whitepaper.
03:34 Tom Hartwell: any third-party pen test reports or bug bounty?
03:38 Alex Reed: we run regular third-party pen tests and have a vulnerability disclosure program; can include high-level summaries in the pack.
03:46 Maya Chen: ok, can you also share your key rotation and KMS auditability? we need to confirm key lifecycle.
03:54 Priya Nair: yes, with customer-managed KMS we defer rotation policy to your KMS, and we maintain access logs showing KMS API calls; for provider-managed keys we rotate per best practices and we can share rotation cadence.
04:12 Tom Hartwell: about data residency — our data must stay in EU for certain projects. do you have region restrictions?
04:20 Alex Reed: Redwood has region support — hosted can be regionally segmented, dedicated deployments can be placed in region, and private is entirely in-customer control. we'll include region availability matrix.
04:35 Maya Chen: compliance artifacts — do you allow us to run an audit or ingest your audit logs into our SIEM?
04:44 Priya Nair: yes, audit logs can be exported to your SIEM or S3 for dedicated/private. for hosted we'll provide log exports and can set up a retention export workflow.
04:58 Leo Park: i need specifics on rate-limiting and token-level cost visibility since our billing team will ask.
05:06 Alex Reed: we'll share our console screenshots and cost breakdown reports.
05:12 Tom Hartwell: what about model and prompt data — do you persist prompts and outputs? i.e., does hosted keep training data?
05:22 Priya Nair: by default hosted stores request logs to improve quality and for debugging, but we have controls to disable retention and an enterprise contract option for no-persist; dedicated and private are under your control so you can choose not to persist outputs.
05:44 Maya Chen: we will likely need private or dedicated for regs but want to see the delta in operational effort and cost.
05:52 Alex Reed: totally — typical tradeoff: hosted is lowest ops but less control over infra/KMS, dedicated gives isolation and predictable throughput, private gives max control for compliance but more ops. we'll send a delta doc and a cost/ops comparison.
06:10 Tom Hartwell: can you do a pilot? we want to run representative workloads and measure latency and throughput with our data residency constraints.
06:18 Priya Nair: yes, we do pilots — for security we'll sign an NDA and scoped data handling. for benchmarking we can run on dedicated or private depending on requirements.
06:30 Maya Chen: question on RBAC auditability — do you record admin actions like who rotated keys or changed roles?
06:38 Priya Nair: yes, admin audit trails are recorded and exportable; we can provide examples.
06:46 Tom Hartwell: any reference customers in pharma?
06:50 Alex Reed: we have a couple in health and biotech — we can share anonymized case studies and contact references with permission.
07:02 Leo Park: integration — our infra team uses Terraform, will Redwood support IaC for dedicated/private deployment?
07:10 Priya Nair: yes, we have Terraform modules and a CLI for private deployments; we'll share repo links and examples.
07:22 Maya Chen: encryption keys — if using BYOK, who has the ability to decrypt? we need proof of separation of duties.
07:31 Priya Nair: with BYOK, keys are in your KMS and Redwood only receives blinded tokens for operational needs; we can go deeper in the security deep dive.
07:45 Tom Hartwell: any specific SLAs around data availability and incident response?
07:52 Alex Reed: dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and latency targets, hosted has standard SLOs and enterprise tiers can add SLAs; incident response details are in our security pack.
08:04 Maya Chen: about legal and data processor agreements — can we get standard DPA and addenda for EU data?
08:10 Alex Reed: yes, we have DPAs, SCCs, and we support EU data agreements; we'll include them in the doc send.
08:22 Tom Hartwell: ok let's recap next steps
08:26 Alex Reed: i will send SOC2 and ISO summary, security deck, and region availability matrix.
08:32 Priya Nair: i'll share SAML/SCIM checklist, sample IdP config, network diagrams, and Terraform modules for private. i'll also draft a benchmark plan.
08:44 Maya Chen: we'll share regulatory scope and provide representative traces and network diagram.
08:50 Tom Hartwell: schedule technical deep dive next week if possible.
08:56 Alex Reed: great — we'll follow up with calendar invites. thanks everyone.
09:02 End of meeting.

Notes about transcription: occasional speaker mis-attribution and filler words present. Some product names transcribed as redwood run-time or redwood private etc.
